findings.description: Static JWT signing key placeholder committed to source control. The literal value 'REPLACE_WITH_A_SECRET_KEY_AT_LEAST_32_CHARS_LONG_abc123xyz' is the HMAC-SHA256 signing key read at startup (Program.cs). Any deployment that does not override it allows an attacker with repo access to forge arbitrary JWT tokens and bypass all [Authorize] endpoints.
findings.consequence: Complete authentication bypass in any environment where Jwt__Key is not overridden via environment variable or secrets manager.
findings.correction: Remove the key value from appsettings.json. Provide it via appsettings.Development.json (git-ignored), dotnet user-secrets, an environment variable (Jwt__Key), or a secrets manager. The existing ?? throw guard in Program.cs is correct and should remain.

findings.description: Live Postgres password committed to source control ('Password=Subh@9899'). Anyone with repo read access obtains the database credential.
findings.consequence: Unauthorized database access if the same password is used on a shared or production Postgres instance.
findings.correction: Move the connection string to appsettings.Development.json (git-ignored), dotnet user-secrets, or the ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection environment variable. Leave only a placeholder in the committed appsettings.json.
